cards.text: Friend, this crowd is HUGE. People are coming to Jesus, God's Son, from town after town, and He tells them a parable. It starts simple: a farmer goes out to sow his seed.

cards.question: As the farmer sows, some seed falls along the path. What happens to it?

answers.text: It gets trampled and eaten by birds
It sinks in and sprouts overnight
It washes away in the rain

cards.text: Some seed falls on rocky ground, and it actually comes up. That's me doing a victory hop on my gold base over a batch that looks PERFECT on top, right before I flip one over.

cards.question: The seedlings on the rocky ground wither because they have no ___.
Other seed falls among thorns. True or false: the thorns grow up with the seedlings and choke them.

cards.text: Still other seed falls on good soil, and it springs up and produces a crop. FINALLY, somebody in this story is having a good day.

cards.question: How big is the crop the seed on the good soil produces?
As He says this, Jesus calls out, "He who has ears to hear, let him hear." True or false: He's telling the crowd to really listen and take it in.
Then the disciples of Jesus come to Him with a question about the farmer and the seed. What do they ask?

cards.text: Honestly, RESPECT, because every one of us has nodded through a whole meeting and then whispered to a coworker, "Wait, what did we just agree to?" The disciples skip all that and go straight to Jesus, and He answers them.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus tells His disciples that the knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of God has been given to them.

cards.text: Jesus says He speaks to others in parables so that, "though seeing, they may not see; though hearing, they may not understand." Hold on to your apron, friend, because this one's worth chewing on.
Now Jesus explains what the parable means, and friend, I LOVE an answer key. I spent years in a junk drawer full of instruction manuals, and not ONE of them ever explained anything.

cards.question: Jesus says the seed in the parable is the ___ of God.

cards.text: First, the seeds along the path, the ones the birds got. Those are people who hear, but then someone comes and takes the word away from their hearts.

cards.question: Who comes and takes the word away from the hearts of the people along the path?

cards.text: He takes it so that they may not believe and be saved. Next up, the rocky ground: people who hear the word and receive it with joy, front row, hands up, the WHOLE thing.

cards.question: The rocky-ground people receive the word with joy, but Jesus says they have no ___.
True or false: when the time of testing comes, the rocky-ground people stand firm.

cards.text: They believe for a season, but in the time of testing, they fall away. Then the thorns: these people hear too, but as they go on their way, they get choked.

cards.question: Jesus says the people among the thorns are choked by the ___, riches, and pleasures of this life.

cards.text: And Jesus says their fruit does not mature. That's me pulling a batch out half-baked because ten other things grabbed my mustache, and friend, it LOOKS like a cookie, but it is NOT a cookie.
And finally, the good soil: people with a noble and good heart who hear the word. These are the ones who produce a crop.

cards.question: What do the good-soil people do with the word they hear?

answers.text: Hear it once and move on

cards.text: Then Jesus switches to a new picture. Someone lights a lamp.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says that after lighting a lamp, a person covers it with a jar or puts it under a bed.

cards.text: Of course not, he sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light. Hiding it would be like baking a perfect batch and shoving it in the back of a junk drawer, and trust me, I KNOW what that drawer does to things.

cards.question: Jesus keeps going about hidden and concealed things. What does He say happens to them?

answers.text: They will all be brought to light
They will fade and be forgotten

cards.question: Remember "He who has ears to hear"? Now Jesus wraps up. What does He tell them to pay attention to?

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "Whoever has will be given more," and then He flips it around. Lean in for this last one, friend.

cards.question: Jesus says that whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has will be ___ from him.

findings.problem: The card identifies Jesus as God's Son, but its only citation is Luke 8:4-5, which does not state that. This outside Bible fact needs its own reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The preceding card only says that Jesus is explaining the parable. It gives the baker no basis for reasoning out that the seed is the word of God rather than the peace or temple of God, so the blank asks for wording the baker has not seen.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card cites only Luke 8:12 but also tells that the birds got the seed along the path, a detail from Luke 8:5. Its citation does not cover everything the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
